I probably omitted some of them, but I can't recall them. But you can find more names in the documentation drawn up at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: These individuals you just mentioned, were they present when you were telling Lord Owen and Cyrus Vance about the various problems that the non-Serb population was suffering in Banja Luka in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: We acquainted the co-chairmen not only with the situation in Banja Luka but the entire Bosnian Krajina, and after that while they were still in the offices and conference rooms, it was offered to hold parallel with the talks press conferences. I don't know whether we were the first, and I was accompanied by Mr. Hadjagic vice-president, and it was approximately as far as the door from the co-chairmen. We had a desk facing about 50 reporters from all corners of the former Yugoslavia, but also many foreign reporters, and if I can draw a comparison to make it clearer, we stated at that press conference verbatim, everything that we had told the co-chairmen, so our communication with them was completely transparent and open to the public, and it could be broadcast not only in Banja Luka, but worldwide, truly worldwide because there were reporters from the US, France, Switzerland, Germany, from all over the world. So indirectly or directly, if you wish, while we were waiting our turn to speak to Mr. Vance and Mr. Owen, we familiarised them with the situation with their own -- in their own territory, conditionally speaking their own territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Just to clarify, this press conference where you reiterated all these problems that were occurring for the non-Serb population in Banja Luka, were the Bosnian Serb officials also present at that press conference?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were sitting behind the reporters. They had not left the hall. They did not leave. In order to leave they would have to pass by us because that was the only exit from that amphitheatre. And I have to correct you on one point, if you allow me. We did not discuss only problems because we use the word problem mainly to talk about minor things, this was about genocide. At that conference information was given loud and clear about the Omarska camp, Manjaca camp, Susica near Mrkonic Grad. About the concentration camp of Trnopolje and the massacres when hundreds of women, children, and men were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to move on to one final topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And if we could bring up what has been admitted now as P459.10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, we heard some evidence about SJB chief Tutus could you ask the witness he was SJB chief where?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Mr. Krzic, you just heard the Judge's question. Do you recall for what municipality was SJB chief Tutus the chief of?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: I think it's the municipality of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, we are of moving --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: My problem is, I don't find Banja Luka SJB on the chart so I didn't find SJB chief Tutus.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We'll have to look at those charts. Banja Luka is one of the indicted municipalities, and it should be there. We'll correct it if there's a mistake. Sorry about that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to just briefly cover the issue of Vecici in Kotor Varos. You testified in Brdjanin that you were involved in the negotiations with the non-Serbs in that village. What we have before you is a report that you wrote that's part of your prior statement that discusses this event, these negotiations, but in the interest of time, I want to jump ahead in it and get to a very important point. You describe how you were told to go to Vecici to negotiate with them to surrender in this document, and when you arrived in Kotor Varos before going to Vecici you met with some Bosnian Serb officials. We would like to verify is that at that meeting in Kotor Varos, which Bosnian Serb officials were present?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: When I arrived there, together with another Bosniak on the Executive Board of the SDA, and together with representatives of the HDZ, I met Colonel Peulic for the first time, and also Mr. Balaban. I can't recall his first name now, but I recognised him from knowing his brother, a doctor in Banja Luka, very well. Then there was Mr. Zupljanin, also Mr. Zdravko Pejic, a police commander in Kotor Varos covering also the territory of surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: To clarify, when you say "Mr. Zupljanin," is that the accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Do you stand behind the information you provide in this report as you testify today?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes, if I can see -- well, this is my own report, although I'd like to see the second page as well, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, could we look at the second page. And perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: You are looking for the signature?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could look at the last page then. There it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is my report done within 24 hours after the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to look at 65 ter Exhibit 10215.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, is this document being tendered as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: That's right, it's already in. This is part of his 92 ter package.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Now, if you could just take a look at this document. Did you receive a copy of this document in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: I think I got the original, or one of the originals, because as far as I can remember, there was an accompanying report with this decision which I can't see here. There was an accompanying document indicating even the colour of the stamp. Anyway, I got this document from a person who was in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Could you tell us who you got this document from and who he was?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Is that absolutely necessary?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, perhaps can we go into private session, and he provides the name, if there's a -- that is a valid concern that this is a person who is not before this Tribunal who might have some security interests that we don't know about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, I believe the rules are and the jurisprudence is clear about this, the Prosecution have to ask to amend the 65 ter list first and then we would be given the opportunity to object or not object and then Your Honours will decide. Now, I understand this is a shortcut, but I believe my learned friend will follow up the procedure by asking for amendment of the 65 ter list. As far as the Stanisic Defence is concerned, we do not object to this document being admitted to 65 ter list and to evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No objection for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Without having to repeat the rules which Mr. Zecevic has kindly reminded you of, Mr. Olmsted, on your application by motion without notice to admit this document -- to include this document on your 65 ter list and thus enable it to be admitted as an exhibit, there being no objection from the other side, the document may be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And just one administrative matter. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P469, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Seems to be my trend today, to interrupt. Just as an administrative matter, I showed him the document before, this was an article. It was 65 ter Exhibit 10214. We just asked that be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Then, Your Honours, the Prosecution is done asking questions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 10214 will become P470 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, what is the reason why you wish to have the article tendered for -- marked for identification? Because normally when we do MFI pieces of evidence, we do it pending something, and so what do you expect shall happen to allow the Chamber to finally admit or possibly admit this article into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, given the objections raised by the Defence regarding other articles, this one was more just for context purposes but at this stage we thought we'll mark it for identification just so it's on the record with a P number in case we need to refer to it again with another witness if it comes up. Obviously there are other names mentioned in there, some who may or may not be witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It seems to us that it would simplify matters if the document were admitted as an exhibit at this stage and it may be so entered and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, in that case, Your Honour, I would welcome the opportunity to object again on the very same reasons why I objected earlier to newspaper articles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So sequentially your -- you repeat the objections that you have made in respect to similar matters today that is noted for the record. Thank you Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And Zupljanin Defence is also supporting this position, for the sake of the [indiscernible] of time we didn't raise after Stanisic Defence but for the record we are supporting this position. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, and the record would so note.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I proceed with the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you gave a certain amount of statements to the OTP beginning with 1994 to date?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: One of the statements was given in December 2000 and in February 2001, do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: I don't know which statement you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about your statement, your witness statement, the one you signed.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: If it's signed by me, then I understand. I thought you were talking about a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to suggest that to be fair to the witness we give him a copy of his statement in a language he understands so he can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, this statement is 1D03-0002 in e-court. This is a statement by this witness from 2000 and 2001. [Trial Chamber and legal officer confer]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The Chamber feels a bit uncomfortable -- right, here it is, thank you very much. We can now see the document. We thought that you were going to have a long discussion --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I just provided the hard copy to the witness in all fairness to him in order that he can shuffle through it, and the document is in e-court with the proper number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, did you have a look at the statement, is it your statement from 2000, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: The first page that I can see indeed is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Look at the last page to see your signature and your confirmation.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: There's no signature, but I suppose that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There's no signature because you only signed the English version of the statement?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember all the details. You are probably right. I signed only the English version because there was no time to have it translated then and there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me then show you your statement in English to verify the signature. Just confirm this is your signature.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Look at the last page or the one but last.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the English version have the same dates as the one I gave you before?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher give me back the English statement to avoid confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you recall, it's a very detailed statement over 40 pages?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: On balance I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the facts from the relevant time that you described and in addition to your answers to specific questions, you also provided clarification of certain documents as well as passages from your book?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That statement is not part of the 92 ter package and therefore I must ask you, do you stand by the statement that you gave as being truthful and that you replied truthfully to all you signed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: I always strove to gave truthful answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So we have no reason to doubt that anything contained in that statement is not true?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: But I must say that as far as I remember during the trial here once there was discussion, but I don't remember the exact case, when a discrepancy between the English translation and the Bosnian one was identified, and it was clarified here in a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand you. But apart from these inadvertent mistakes, the facts mentioned in the statement are generally correct; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Witness, you were the president of the SDA, of the Banja Luka municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I remember well, you were in that position from 1991 on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: To be more precise, from the end of 1991 onward.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the initiative launched by the SDA and implemented in the territory of the Banja Luka municipality about the separation of some parts of the Banja Luka municipality and they becoming separate municipalities? When I say that, I'm referring to the part of the Banja Luka municipality called Stari Grad old town, which is a part of Banja Luka city, and the settlement of Ivanjska in the Banja Luka municipality, according to that SDA initiative separate municipalities were to be established there toward the end of 1991 or in early 1992, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, but I stress the fact that these were only initiatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see Exhibit P460 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's the map, sir, that you were looking at today with my learned friend the Prosecutor, so if you can identify the Stari Grad part of Banja Luka, can you please mark it with the pen that you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I misquoted. I would like to see 65 ter 10213. So as to avoid confusing the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I say something before I do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, that initiative wasn't precise in terms of territory. I can't remember the local communities in question, I can only roughly outline the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You will show us on the map once we see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 10213. Your Honours, we have this map which is marked P460. Oh, now we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see it? This is the map that the OTP showed you earlier today and just approximately because it isn't essential, show me which part of Banja Luka the Stari Grad is which under the SDA initiative should have become a separate municipality.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: I believe that one part of this planned municipality of Stari Grad is not shown here. It's along the right bank of the Vrbas River toward Seher.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay, then do mark the part that can be seen on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And now to make it completely clear, can you mark the part that was supposed to become part of the new municipality, could you mark it with lines?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the part that you marked with the blue pen would be part of the municipality that was the object of the SDA initiative that should have been separated from Banja Luka and become a separate municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: No. This territory -- yes, it is this territory, but the rest of what you said is not true. Can I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, it was not a pure SDA initiative. It was a joint initiative in which the HDZ took part and the leftist parties as -- are something, I don't -- whatever it's called, and then the planned municipality of Stari Grad shouldn't have been taken out of Banja Luka. The aim was the re-organisation of the bulkiest municipality in former Yugoslavia in line with the European principles.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, allow me to interrupt you. I asked you a very concrete question so kindly answer it because our time is limited. This isn't this significant. I know I'm asking the question, and I asked you whether what you marked in blue on this map represents part of the Stari Grad municipality, and the SDA was one of those who initiated its creation, irrespective of the intention of with whether it was supposed to become a separate municipality or community of municipalities or anything else?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: I must add something else, that there was an initiative board headed by experts, but I wasn't part of that board, and from that aspect I was not familiar with the exact limits of the municipality, but I did know that all the municipalities were multi-ethnic and this one in question was Serb dominated, were the Serb majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I do kindly ask you to listen to my question. What you have marked with the blue pen, is that part of the planned municipality of Stari Grad in 1991 or 1992, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: With a probability of 70 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D154, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please show to the witness, 65 ter 3144.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you can see this map here, the one on the left is the map of the Banja Luka municipality isn't it, roughly?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, let me first ask you, there was also an initiative for Ivanjska to become a separate municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, but if you want to ask me about the borders, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking about the borders, I'm only asking about geographical notions. So the settlement of Ivanjska, is it right that others were also planned such as Stricici?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then Centar; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Krupa na Vrbasu; right?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Bronzani Majdan?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you now use the same blue pen to mark these geographical entities on the map. Ivanjska, Centar, Krupa na Vrbasu, Bronzani Majdan and Stricici, if you know where they are, approximately of course, just mark circles.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: That's Ivanjska. I don't think that Stricici is marked here but I can approximately mark where it is located. And what else did you mention?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Krupa na Vrbasu?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: You said Centar approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So these are approximately the municipalities to be newly established?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Stari Grad isn't marked here as it should be hereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please do add Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document with the witness's marks into evidence unless the OTP object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D155, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that in some of these parts of the Banja Luka municipality that were envisaged to become new municipalities, and in the community of municipalities or association of municipalities of Banja Luka, the Croats and Muslims were the majority population?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: I don't believe that in any municipality the Bosniaks are the majority population. I'm not sure that this applies to Ivanj ska though because these supposed municipalities all have a mixed population, so I doubt that anywhere there would be an absolute majority of one ethnicity. Whereas in the other municipalities that was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Which other municipalities are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Well, if you speak about Stricici and the centre of town and even the so-called Stari Grad municipality was predominantly Serb populated. You could tell by the number of representatives in the town Assembly. And I'm convinced that the Serbs were the majority there. So the intention was not to separate ethnicities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then what was the intention behind this fragmentation of Banja Luka municipality?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Even then experts irrespective of their ethnicity wanted to help Banja Luka. It wasn't actually us. That was an initiative that goes back to communist Yugoslavia. The survey was made during communist Yugoslavia and one of the authors was Dr. Osmanovic who also participated here. So this all stemmed from an economic survey which was made during communist Yugoslavia, and as you know, communist Yugoslavia never --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I must interrupt you. Communist Yugoslavia is no concern of ours here. I would like you to answer my question. You remember that you were criticized at the time in early 1992 that is, that you are creating municipalities with a Muslim majority out of parts of the then Banja Luka municipality, do you remember that? Were you criticised, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: I don't remember such criticism.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But do you remember that you gave an interview to the newspapers and which you say no matter what they are saying it isn't true that we want to create municipalities with a Muslim majority in parts of the Banja Luka municipality?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Well, I would have to see that interview, but isn't that actually corroborating what I said a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm actually wondering why a local journalist is asking you about creating municipalities with a Muslim majority, and you are here telling us that Serbs were the majority in some of these parts?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just show you something to refresh your memory lest somebody should think that I want to confuse you or lead you astray.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please show the witness document 1D03-0156.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see this? Is this an interview you gave, sir? It says on the side 17th of January, 1992, and underneath it says "Muslimanski Glasnik," is that so?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: If I can give you more detailed --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, I just want to know whether you remember this document and whether this is an interview you gave?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: This is an interview that was taken from "Oslobodenje".

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But that's your interview, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: I have to read it first. I have trouble remembering and this is very small.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please enlarge the version in the language that the witness understands, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, you have two minutes before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I know, Your Honours, I just want to deal with this. I'm not offering this as ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is my interview, but what do you want to know?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You see, at the very end of this interview of yours?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: No, I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's under the other document. The last paragraph. And you say here too I want to stress that this isn't about the establishment of Muslim municipalities but about the streamlining of the two big current municipality of Banja Luka, et cetera. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MUHAREM KRZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wanted to deal with another topic now, so this may be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the adjournment to resume in this courtroom tomorrow at 9.00, and I would remind the witness that having been sworn, you cannot communicate with the lawyers from either side in this matter, and in such conversations as you may have with anybody outside the courtroom, you cannot discuss your testimony before the Tribunal. So thank you, sir, you are excused to return at 9.00 tomorrow morning. We rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of January, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.59 p.m.
